To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel method for the purification of alkaline phosphatase, which is a sialoglyco‐protein, and that pyridoxal‐phosphate is a substrate for this enzyme.
we have isolated a novel protein that has the ability to inhibit the growth of a wide variety of bacteria and that the protein is produced by a bacterium that is found in the soil.
the purified alkaline phosphatase is a sialoglycosylated protein with pyridoxal 5′‐phosphate phosphatse activity and that the two activities are mutually competitive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of a brain‐associated protein, the major component of which is the enzyme alkaline phosphatase.
the purification of brain alkaline phosphatase to homogeneity, and the characterization of the homogeneous enzyme.
the purification and characterization of alkaline phosphatase, a glycoprotein enzyme, from sheep brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enzyme from the brain is similar to that from the kidney in its general properties.
the brain alkaline phosphatase is a pyridoxal‐dependent enzyme.
sheep brain alkaline phosphatase is a sialoglycoenzyme containing a single pyridoxal 5′‐phosphate residue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sheep brain alkaline phosphatase is a sialoglyco‐protein with pyridoxal phosphatase activity and is a metal‐containing enzyme with a molecular weight of about 100,000.
alkaline phosphatase of brain is a sialoglyco‐protein which is composed of two nonidentical subunits of MW 70,000 and 55,000.
the enzyme is a pyridoxal‐containing glycoprotein with pyridoxal phosphatase activity and is localized in the cytoplasmic fraction of the brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have purified the enzyme to homogeneity.
the enzyme is an excellent model for the study of the mechanism of alkaline phosphatase.

we have developed a method that allows us to study the effect of different factors on the activity of a particular phosphatase in a specific biological sample, and that this method is useful for studying the activity of phosphatases in general.
